200	Extremely severe. And people, a baal teshuvah, who calls himself a rabbi... Woe
201	to us, "a rabbi for our disputes, and a judge for our cases."
202	Therefore, a person who has holiness and closeness to HaShem must guard it
203	more than anything!
204	You have a dear friend, a merciful Father who loves you.
205	You have a relationship with Him of love, of devotion, of closeness, of speech.
206	Is this the most important thing to you in the world?
207	Don't sell it for a pot of lentil stew.
208	Don't sell it for a pot of lentil stew.
209	And every millimeter forward that you can draw closer in a relationship with Him, even if it costs you blood,
210	tears and fasts, "your heart and your blood", pour it out, pour it out and draw close to Him.
211	The main thing is to be more His friend, closer to Him.
212	Don't they tell about Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, peace be upon him? They called him a chasid, and why was he a chasid? Because every
213	extra piece of piety he could take, he took upon himself. Once Rabbi Efraim Cohen told, and why would he take on pious practices?
214	To cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, to come a little closer to Him, another millimeter. Once he was studying
215	Etz Chaim and didn't understand, reviewed it and didn't understand, opened the window, not knowing
216	that the room was empty. His yeshivah was in Hebron.
217	He was the rabbi of Hebron, and one of the rabbis was there, where the door was
218	open, and he saw the rabbi open the window and say: Master of the worlds, I don't understand. How many
219	fasts have I already fasted, how many self-denials have I already undergone. What more do You want me to take upon myself
220	that I haven't taken? See what this is, where he got to: what more do You
221	want me to take upon myself that I haven't taken?
222	I've already taken on every pious practice I can, I've stretched myself to the limit of my ability.
223	So a person who is a servant of HaShem, who draws close to the Holy One, blessed be He, as much as he can, is strict with himself.
224	Not everything is lenient, everything "they were accustomed to be lenient," these are laws for after the fact.
225	There are those who are experts in the laws of after the fact.
226	After the fact it's possible, but after the fact it's permitted.
227	Haven't I told you already a thousand times that someone calls me,
228	asks me a question, permitted or forbidden. I told him forbidden. He tells me, Rabbi,
229	think again, tell me, are you serious? I tell you
230	forbidden. He says to me, maybe nevertheless you can find some way to permit it. I told him,
231	the Gemara, the Yerushalmi, the Shulchan Aruch and the Rambam all ruled to forbid. He says to me, "Ya Allah, you're
232	already the eighth rabbi to tell me it's forbidden. Have mercy! What are you looking for?
233	A goat in your place to go to Azazel?
234	To go to Gehinnom in your place?
235	What are you, forbidden means forbidden. There are those who are experts in after-the-fact laws.
236	Listen, but after the fact it's permitted, but after the fact there is "they were accustomed to be lenient," but after the fact, but after the fact.
237	Instead of being someone who distances himself from a hundred gates of after-the-fact, for the sake of a hundred
238	gates of permissibility, so as not to stumble in one after-the-fact case.
239	A person who is a servant of HaShem, "on my bed at night, I sought the one my soul loves," seeks still more closeness to HaShem,
